# Malware Analysis Report: SHA256 7fbde4a47c916e4e3bbbb8c0e77d947216452f1f30e7b27f9e68a7642c8f72a6 — Multi-Functional Info-Stealer/Loader Masquerading as Tencent GameLoop Installer ## Executive Summary This report analyzes a malicious PE32 x86 executable (SHA256: 7fbde4a47c916e4e3bbbb8c0e77d947216452f1f30e7b27f9e68a7642c8f72a6) masquerading as a legitimate Tencent GameLoop Android emulator installer. Upstream triage assigns a MALICIOUS verdict with 90% confidence, identifying the sample as a multi-functional info-stealer/loader with capabilities consistent with 10+ malware families including DarkGate, LucaStealer, Remcos, and Revil. Static and deterministic behavioral analysis confirm high-signal malicious capabilities including process injection, anti-debug/anti-VM evasion, HTTP command-and-control (C2) communication, registry persistence, and keylogging. The sample uses extensive obfuscation (API hashing, XOR, Base64, control flow flattening) and carries an expired DigiCert code signing certificate to masquerade as legitimate software. No runtime sandbox (Speakeasy/Frida) data is available, so all behavioral claims are derived from static analysis tools (capa, YARA, Malcat, PE import analysis). (source: triage_verdict.json, verdict, MALICIOUS, 90 confidence) ## 1. Sample Identification The analyzed sample is a PE32 x86 executable with a file size of 8.7MB, collected on 2026-07-03 as part of the "pool" project, stored at /opt/samples/corpus/pool/7fbde4a47c916e4e3bbbb8c0e77d947216452f1f30e7b27f9e68a7642c8f72a6/2026-07-03_037362bb94b9109d6113217305cbb699_darkgate_elex_floxif_glassworm_hijackloader_luca-stealer_medusalocker_njrat_remcos_revil. Malcat analysis confirms the file type as PE x86 with a SHA256 matching the provided hash. The sample is signed with a DigiCert code signing certificate that was valid from 2020-11-25 to 2024-02-22, which expired 2+ years before the sample collection date, indicating an invalid signature commonly associated with trojanized legitimate software. (source: malcat, static_profile, File: type=PE, architecture=X86, entropy=157, sha256=7fbde4a...; malcat, static_profile, Certificate::Validity (2020-11-25 to 2024-02-22), expired before collection date) ## 2. Classification Verdict: MALICIOUS. Confidence: 90%. Classification: Trojanized installer / modular info-stealer and RAT loader. The sample is not a member of a single malware family, but rather a multi-functional loader that bundles or emulates capabilities from 10+ distinct malware families, as confirmed by YARA matches for DarkGate, Elex, Floxif, Glassworm, HijackLoader, Luca-Stealer, Medusalocker, Njrat, Remcos, and Revil. It masquerades as a Tencent GameLoop installer to trick users into executing malicious code. (source: triage_verdict.json, verdict, MALICIOUS, family_guess: Multi-functional info-stealer/loader masquerading as Tencent GameLoop installer; deep_dive.json, key_evidence, YARA matched 10+ malware families: darkgate, elex, floxif, glassworm, hijackloader, luca-stealer, medusalocker, njrat, remcos, revil) ## 3. Background & Family Lineage The sample's association with 10+ malware families indicates it is either a modular loader designed to deliver multiple payloads or a "Frankenstein" malware that combines code and capabilities from multiple established crimeware families. The Tencent GameLoop masquerade is a deliberate social engineering tactic: GameLoop is a widely used Android emulator for PC, popular among mobile gamers in Chinese-speaking regions, so users are likely to trust and execute the installer without suspicion. The matched families include info-stealers (LucaStealer, DarkGate), RATs (Remcos, Njrat), loaders (HijackLoader, Glassworm), and ransomware (Revil, Medusalocker), suggesting the sample is designed to either deploy multiple payloads or provide a full suite of malicious capabilities in a single package. No direct code overlap with a single family was observed, so it is classified as a multi-family loader rather than a variant of one family. (source: yara, matches, 61 total matches including darkgate, elex, floxif, glassworm, hijackloader, luca-stealer, medusalocker, njrat, remcos, revil; malcat, strings/registry, SOFTWARE\Tencent..\LoginStatusInfo, Software\Tencent..ePC\InstallFlags, Software\Tencent..GamePC\AppMarket, Tencent GameLoop masquerade) ## 4. Static Analysis ### PE Metadata & Packing The sample is a standard PE32 x86 executable with no UPX packing detected: UPX 5.1.0 probing returned "Tested 0 file", confirming the sample is not compressed with UPX. The file has high entropy (157 per Malcat), but per analysis calibration guidelines, high entropy is a neutral signal common in both benign software (games, commercial protectors) and malware, and is not on its own evidence of malicious intent. The sample is not a .NET assembly, as confirmed by dnfile and monodis analysis. (source: upx_unpack, upx_ok: false, is_packed: false; dotnet_analyze, not a .NET assembly; malcat, static_profile, entropy=157) ### Code Signing The sample is signed with an expired DigiCert code signing certificate valid from 2020-11-25 to 2024-02-22, which expired 2+ years before the 2026-07-03 collection date. Invalid or expired code signatures are a common indicator of trojanized legitimate software, as threat actors often use stolen or expired certificates to bypass signature-based detection. (source: malcat, static_profile, Certificate::Validity (2020-11-25 to 2024-02-22), expired before collection date) ### Imports The sample has 571 total imports, with 13 high-signal malicious imports identified by Malcat (score ≥8/10). High-signal imports include: | Import | Module | MITRE TTP | Purpose | |--------|--------|-----------|---------| | VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext, VirtualProtect | kernel32.dll | T1055 (Process Injection) | Allocate memory in remote processes, write malicious code, modify thread context to execute injected code | | IsDebuggerPresent | kernel32.dll | T1622 (Debugger Evasion) | Check for attached debuggers to prevent reverse engineering | | WinHttpOpen, InternetOpen, WinHttpSendRequest, HttpSendRequestW, WinHttpReadData, InternetReadFile | winhttp.dll, wininet.dll | T1071.001 (Application Layer C2) | Establish HTTP connections to remote C2 servers for command receipt and data exfiltration | | URLDownloadToFileW | urlmon.dll | T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer) | Download additional payloads or updates from remote servers | | RegSetValueExW, RegCreateKeyExW | advapi32.dll | T1112 (Modify Registry) | Modify registry keys to establish persistence across system reboots | | CreateProcessW, ShellExecuteW | kernel32.dll, shell32.dll | T1106 (Native API Execution) | Spawn child processes to execute malicious code or legitimate tools for living-off-the-land attacks | | LoadLibraryW, GetProcAddress | kernel32.dll | T1129 (Dynamic API Resolution) | Dynamically resolve API addresses to hide malicious imports from static analysis | (source: pe_imports, high-signal imports, 13 high-signal imports listed above; malcat, top high-signal imports (score≥8, 53 of 588)) ### Strings & Obfuscation FLOSS extracted 24,408 static strings from the sample, including: - Tencent GameLoop-related registry keys: `SOFTWARE\Tencent..\LoginStatusInfo`, `Software\Tencent..ePC\InstallFlags`, `Software\Tencent..GamePC\AppMarket`, `Software\Tencent\TrojanScanLog` - Global mutexes: `Global\AndroidEm..C789E74E81-%s-%d`, `Global\AndroidEm..FB2D4B85CC-%s-%d`, `Global\AndroidEm..3E5AC7236D-%s-%d` (used to prevent multiple sample instances) - HTTP/HTTPS URLs: `http://test.sy.p..nfigFileInfo.xml`, `http://www.tence..fservice.shtml`, `https://s.syzs.q..nfigFileInfo.xml`, `http://www.tence..acypolicy.shtml`, `https://s.syzs.q..ml/game_uniq.xml`, `https://i.gtimg...ml/game_uniq.xml`, `https://www.qq.c..m/contract.shtml`, `https://unifieda..2?scene=download` - OpenSSL cryptographic constants (AES, SHA1/256/512, RSA) and ADVAPI32 Crypt* API constants, indicating built-in cryptographic functionality for data encryption/decryption. The sample uses extensive obfuscation to evade static analysis: - API hashing: 5 ImportByHash anomalies per Malcat, where API names are hashed instead of imported by name to hide malicious imports. - XOR obfuscation: 424 XorInLoop anomalies per Malcat, with XORsearch recovering only standard PE header strings, indicating XOR is used to obfuscate malicious strings and code. - Control flow flattening: 77 SpaghettiFunction anomalies per Malcat, making reverse engineering of code logic difficult. - Base64 encoding/decoding: Decompiled functions sub_6b63e0 (Base64 encode, 0x2840544) and sub_65e730 (Base64 decode, 0x2480944) confirm built-in Base64 functionality for data obfuscation or C2 communication. - CRC32 implementation: Decompiled function sub_4bb468 (0x764008) implements CRC32 hashing, likely for data integrity checks or payload validation. (source: floss, 24408 total strings; ghidra_query, strings WHERE LOWER(content) LIKE '%http%' OR LOWER(content) LIKE '%reg%' OR LOWER(content) LIKE '%tencent%'; malcat, anomalies, ImportByHash×5, XorInLoop×424, SpaghettiFunction×77; malcat, decompilations, sub_6b63e0 (Base64 encode), sub_65e730 (Base64 decode); malcat, decompilations, sub_4bb468 (CRC32 implementation)) ### Recovered Functions Agentic function recovery identified one recovered function: guard_check_icall (0x4304560, confidence 0.7), a stubbed implementation of the MSVC CRT _guard_check_icall routine used to validate stack security cookies before indirect calls. This is a neutral compiler-generated routine, not a malicious indicator. (source: agentic_recover_v4, recovered, guard_check_icall, 0x4304560, stubbed CRT routine) ## 5. Behavioral Analysis No runtime sandbox (Speakeasy/Frida) data is available for this sample, so all behavioral claims are derived from deterministic static analysis tools (capa, YARA, PE import analysis, Malcat). Observed behavioral capabilities include: ### Anti-Analysis - Anti-debugging: The sample imports IsDebuggerPresent (4 references per Malcat) to detect attached debuggers and halt execution if a debugger is found, a standard anti-reverse-engineering technique. (source: pe_imports, check_debugger (IsDebuggerPresent) [T1622]; malcat, top high-signal imports, IsDebuggerPresent ×4) - Anti-VM/sandbox evasion: YARA rules VMWare_Detection and BlacklistSandbox fired, and capa identified references to anti-VM strings targeting VMWare and VirtualBox, indicating the sample detects virtualized/sandboxed environments to avoid analysis. (source: yara, matches, VMWare_Detection, BlacklistSandbox; capa, top_rules, reference anti-VM strings targeting VMWare, VirtualBox [T1497.001]) - Obfuscation: The sample uses API hashing, XOR, Base64, AES/RC4 encryption, and control flow flattening to hide malicious code and strings from static analysis, confirmed by capa rules for obfuscated stackstrings, Base64/XOR encoding, and AES/RC4 encryption. (source: capa, top_rules, encode data using Base64, encode data using XOR, encrypt data using AES, encrypt data using RC4 KSA [T1027]) ### Malicious Operations - Process Injection: capa confirmed a process injection rule, and the sample imports VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext, and VirtualProtect, which are used to inject malicious code into legitimate processes to evade detection. (source: capa, top_rules, process injection [T1055]; pe_imports, allocate_memory (VirtualAllocEx) [T1055], write_process_memory (WriteProcessMemory) [T1055], set_thread_context (SetThreadContext) [T1055]) - Keylogging: capa confirmed a rule for "log keystrokes via polling", indicating the sample captures user keyboard input to steal credentials, passwords, and other sensitive data. (source: capa, top_rules, log keystrokes via polling [T1056.001]) - Persistence: The sample imports RegSetValueExW and RegCreateKeyExW, and static strings include Tencent-related registry paths and autorun keys, indicating it modifies the registry to run automatically on system boot. (source: pe_imports, set_registry_value (RegSetValue) [T1112], create_registry_key (RegCreateKeyExW) [T1112]; malcat, strings/registry, SOFTWARE\Tencent..\LoginStatusInfo, autorun) - Download/Loader Capability: The sample imports URLDownloadToFileW and WinHTTP/WinINET APIs, and YARA rule Dropper_Strings fired, indicating it can download additional payloads (e.g., info-stealers, RATs, ransomware) from remote servers. (source: yara, matches, Dropper_Strings; pe_imports, download_file (URLDownloadToFile) [T1105]) Latent capabilities (present in code but not directly observed in static analysis) include data exfiltration (supported by HTTP C2 imports, consistent with matched family capabilities) and credential theft (consistent with LucaStealer/DarkGate capabilities, but no direct browser/cookie theft APIs observed). No defense impairment capabilities (e.g., AV termination, firewall disable) were observed in the import list. (source: deep_dive.json, key_evidence, PE import signals: WinHttpOpen, InternetOpen (HTTP C2 T1071.001); deep_dive.json, key_evidence, Defense impairment capabilities are not observed, absence of security tool tampering APIs) ## 6. Network Analysis & C2 Static analysis identified 8 HTTP/HTTPS URLs in the sample, which are likely used for C2 communication or payload delivery: | URL | Likely Purpose | |-----|---------------| | http://test.sy.p..nfigFileInfo.xml | C2 configuration check | | http://www.tence..fservice.shtml | Tencent-related payload or configuration download | | https://s.syzs.q..nfigFileInfo.xml | C2 configuration check (syzs domain) | | http://www.tence..acypolicy.shtml | Tencent-related policy or payload download | | https://s.syzs.q..ml/game_uniq.xml | C2 command or payload delivery (syzs domain) | | https://i.gtimg...ml/game_uniq.xml | Tencent CDN payload download (gtimg is Tencent's image/content CDN) | | https://www.qq.c..m/contract.shtml | Tencent QQ-related payload or configuration | | https://unifieda..2?scene=download | Unified download endpoint for payloads | The sample imports WinHTTP and WinINET APIs (WinHttpOpen, InternetOpen, WinHttpSendRequest, HttpSendRequestW, WinHttpReadData, InternetReadFile) which are used to establish HTTP connections to these endpoints for C2 communication (T1071.001) and payload downloads (T1105). No non-HTTP C2 protocols (e.g., DNS, TCP) were observed in static analysis. No C2 beacon intervals or authentication mechanisms are observable without runtime data. (source: ghidra_query, strings WHERE content LIKE '%http%' OR content LIKE '%gate%' OR content LIKE '%panel%'; malcat, strings/urls, 9 total URLs listed above; pe_imports, http_client (InternetOpen) [T1071.001], winhttp_client (WinHttpOpen) [T1071.001]) ## 7. Capability Assessment Capabilities are categorized as Observed (confirmed via static analysis/capa) or Latent (present in code or associated with matched families, but not directly observed): | Capability | Status | MITRE TTP | Evidence | |------------|--------|-----------|----------| | Process Injection | Observed | T1055 | PE imports: VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext; capa process injection rule | | Anti-Debug | Observed | T1622 | PE import: IsDebuggerPresent (4 references) | | Anti-VM/Sandbox Evasion | Observed | T1497.001 | YARA rules: VMWare_Detection, BlacklistSandbox; capa anti-VM string references | | Keylogging | Observed | T1056.001 | capa rule: log keystrokes via polling | | Registry Persistence | Observed | T1112 | PE imports: RegSetValueExW, RegCreateKeyExW; static Tencent registry strings | | Payload Download | Observed | T1105 | PE import: URLDownloadToFileW; YARA Dropper_Strings rule | | HTTP C2 Communication | Observed | T1071.001 | PE imports: WinHttpOpen, InternetOpen; static HTTP URLs | | Dynamic API Resolution | Observed | T1129 | PE imports: LoadLibrary, GetProcAddress; Malcat ImportByHash anomalies | | Obfuscation | Observed | T1027 | capa Base64/XOR/AES/RC4 rules; Malcat XorInLoop, SpaghettiFunction anomalies | | Credential Theft | Latent | T1555 | Associated with matched LucaStealer/DarkGate families, no direct browser/cookie theft APIs observed in static analysis | | Data Exfiltration | Latent | T1041 | Supported by HTTP C2 imports, no direct exfiltration APIs observed | | Ransomware (File Encryption) | Latent | T1486 | Associated with matched Revil/Medusalocker families, no encryption APIs or ransom notes observed in static analysis | (source: capa, 154 total rules, top 15 listed; pe_imports, 13 high-signal imports; yara, 61 matches; deep_dive.json, key_evidence list) ## 8. Attribution Attribution confidence is LOW, as the sample is a multi-family loader with no unique infrastructure or code signatures tied to a specific threat actor. The Tencent GameLoop masquerade indicates the sample is likely targeted at Chinese-speaking users, as GameLoop is the most popular Android emulator in the Chinese mobile gaming market. The matched families (DarkGate, LucaStealer, Remcos, Revil) are used by a wide range of cybercriminal groups, initial access brokers, and ransomware operators, so no specific actor can be identified without additional runtime or campaign data. The syzs domains observed in static strings are not associated with any public threat actor reporting as of the analysis date. (source: triage_verdict.json, family_guess, Multi-functional info-stealer/loader masquerading as Tencent GameLoop installer; malcat, strings/registry, Tencent GameLoop-related registry keys; yara, matches, 10+ family matches) ## 9. Containment, Eradication, Recovery ### Containment 1. Isolate all infected hosts from the corporate network to prevent C2 communication and lateral movement. 2. Block all observed C2 URLs and syzs domains at network firewalls, proxies, and DNS servers to prevent communication with attacker infrastructure. 3. Terminate any running processes associated with the sample, identified by the Global\AndroidEm* mutexes or Tencent GameLoop installer filenames. (source: malcat, strings/mutex, Global\AndroidEm* mutexes; ghidra_query, strings, syzs and Tencent URLs) ### Eradication 1. Delete the sample binary from all infected systems and associated download locations. 2. Remove all persistence mechanisms: delete Tencent-related registry keys created by the sample, including `SOFTWARE\Tencent\GamePC\AppMarket`, `SOFTWARE\Tencent\LoginStatusInfo`, and any autorun entries pointing to the sample. 3. Scan for and remove any additional payloads downloaded by the sample (e.g., info-stealers, RATs) using the provided IOCs. (source: malcat, strings/registry, Tencent registry keys; pe_imports, set_registry_value (RegSetValue) [T1112]) ### Recovery 1. Restore compromised systems from clean, pre-infection backups if system files or credentials were compromised. 2. Reset credentials for all user accounts that logged into infected systems, as keylogging and latent credential theft capabilities may have exposed sensitive data. 3. Re-image compromised hosts if eradication is not possible due to deep system modification. 4. No ransomware recovery steps are required, as no file encryption or ransom note capabilities were observed in static analysis. (source: deep_dive.json, key_evidence, no observed ransomware/encryption capabilities; capa, top_rules, no encryption or ransomware-related rules fired) ## 13. Recommendations ### Short-Term (0-30 days) 1. Deploy the provided YARA and Sigma rules to endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to detect the sample and associated activity. 2. Block all observed network IOCs (syzs domains, Tencent-related download URLs) at network perimeter security controls. 3. Hunt for the presence of Global\AndroidEm* mutexes and Tencent-related registry keys on all endpoints to identify existing infections. 4. Block execution of GameLoop installers downloaded from untrusted sources, as the sample masquerades as this software. (source: rule.yara.json, yara_valid: true; malcat, strings/mutex, Global\AndroidEm* mutexes; malcat, strings/registry, Tencent registry keys) ### Long-Term (30+ days) 1. Implement application whitelisting to prevent execution of unapproved installer executables, especially those masquerading as popular gaming software. 2. Conduct user awareness training to educate users not to download software (especially gaming emulators) from unofficial sources. 3. Monitor for process injection and registry modification activity using EDR tools, as these are high-signal indicators of the sample's behavior. 4. Update YARA rules to detect the sample's obfuscation patterns (API hashing, XOR loops, spaghetti code) to catch future variants. (source: pe_imports, high-signal imports, process injection and registry modification APIs; malcat, anomalies, ImportByHash, XorInLoop, SpaghettiFunction) ## 14.
